title: AI Models Are Getting Harder to Monitor, Says U.K. Government’s Joseph Bloom
summary: The ability to monitor AI models to detect what they’re trying to do and why is widely considered a crucial part of the effort to keep the technology operating safely. It’s also increasingly hard to do, said Joseph Bloom, the head of model transparency at the U.K. AI Security Institute.“In general, we’re seeing monitorability—in various respects or from various angles—decrease,” Bloom said on the latest episode of The Information’s AI Deep Dive, in one of the first on-the-record interviews that a member of technical staff at AISI has given. (The full episode is available here.) The institute is one of the world’s largest government bodies focused on AI, and its work includes evaluating models from leading AI companies.

bajada: El jefe de transparencia del Instituto de Seguridad de IA del Reino Unido advierte que monitorear modelos para detectar sus comportamientos es cada vez más difícil. La falta de interpretabilidad plantea desafíos críticos para la regulación y seguridad de IA.
bajada_en: The U.K. AI Security Institute's head of model transparency warns that monitoring AI models to understand their behavior is increasingly difficult. Lack of interpretability poses critical challenges for AI regulation and safety.

title: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents
summary:
arXiv:2611.00244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. A common approach is compaction, where the model replaces its history with a self-generated note. Yet off-the-shelf agentic models, including GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.3, often write ineffective notes, and reinforcement learning (RL) alone rarely discovers useful note-taking behavior. We present MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B and trained to manage its context through compaction. We first bootstrap note-taking by fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, then reinforce it with RL using a reward that combines answer correctness, note-quality heuristics, and confidence calibration. Although trained only to compact into a fresh window, MEMENTO extends at test time to strategies such as context folding and confidence-based backtracking. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, with books of up to 2.5M tokens, MEMENTO raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context. It outperforms GPT-5.5 agent in the same harness (13.1%) and full book context (56.7%) at less than 1/50 the cost. It also nearly matches a ~100x larger GLM-5.3 agent (69.3%) at 1/9 the cost, and comes within 6.4 points of GLM-5.3 full context at 1/26 the cost.
title_es: MEMENTO: gestión inteligente de contexto para agentes con documentos largos
bajada: Investigadores presentan MEMENTO, un agente que aprende a gestionar contexto mediante compactación de notas, procesando documentos de hasta 2.5M tokens. Avance significativo para agentes que operan sobre entradas muy largas sin perder información crítica.
bajada_en: Researchers introduce MEMENTO, an agent that learns context management through note-taking, processing documents up to 2.5M tokens. Significant advance for agents operating on very long inputs without losing critical information.

title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
summary:
arXiv:2611.00172v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Embedding models underpin virtually every modern AI system, from search engines to recommendation systems. Despite shared mathematical foundations, research on embedding models remains fragmented by modality: the communities develop largely in isolation, seldom exchanging insights. We argue that this fragmentation obscures a deeper convergence. Driven by contrastive learning, Transformer architectures, and a granularity shift, embedding research across modalities is converging toward a common set of principles, even as modality-specific challenges remain underexplored. To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities: coverage, comparability, and compositionality. Three paths toward unification satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus we advocate, aims at compositionality. This position paper traces the resulting evolution, providing the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research.
title_es: Estudio: convergencia hacia embeddings omnimodales unificados
bajada: Un nuevo paper traza la convergencia de investigación en embeddings multimodales, proponiendo un framework hacia embeddings conjuntos que combinen visión, texto y audio. El trabajo unifica fragmentación histórica en investigación de embeddings por modalidad.
bajada_en: A new paper traces convergence in multimodal embeddings research, proposing a framework toward joint embeddings combining vision, text, and audio. The work unifies historical fragmentation in embeddings research by modality.
